blocks.why: Normal night at home to bank sleep before the month starts with a westbound all-nighter.
Afternoon nap before a 21:50 local push to Bogota — this is the sleep that gets me through top of descent.
Straight to bed off the aeroplane at 02:30 local Bogota; it's body-morning so I'll take whatever I get.
The proper Bogota night sleep, the one real anchor of this layover.
Early-afternoon top-up before the 17:10 local pickup for another twelve-hour night home.
Home mid-afternoon after an overnight; short nap only, so I can still sleep tonight and reset to Madrid time.
Full night at home to put the body clock back on Madrid before the standby block.
Insurance nap before a standby that can run to 02:00 local.
Sleep in after the standby released at 02:00 local — protect the length, the timing is already lost.
A long deliberate nap before evening standby, because tomorrow's Boston report leaves almost no night.
Only three and a quarter hours in bed between standby release and the commute — this is the squeeze, and it is why the afternoon nap mattered.
Short lie-down on arrival in Boston to take the edge off, then back up so I can sleep this evening.
Long sleep starting 18:00 local Boston, which is midnight body time — the best-aligned window of the whole layover.
Four hours in the Boston afternoon before a 23:10 local red-eye; going to work with fresh sleep rather than a whole day awake.
Home early afternoon off the red-eye; capped at three hours so tonight still works.
Full Madrid night to re-anchor before two nights of late standby.
Nap before a standby that runs to 04:00 local.
Sleep after the overnight standby releases; dark room, phone off.
Same again before the second night standby, which finishes even later.
Post-standby sleep on my day off, finishing by lunchtime so I can go to bed early tonight.
Lights out at 20:00 local for a 05:05 local report — an early start is won or lost the evening before.
Ten hours after a four-sector day that started before dawn; no nap today, just an early night.
Ordinary night off — banking sleep while the roster lets me.
Full night before the Dubai sector; nothing clever needed, it's a daytime duty.
Dubai local night is only two hours off my body clock, so a straight eight hours in the hotel works.
Top-up before the evening pickup, since we land Madrid near midnight body time.
Home from Dubai at 01:35 local and straight to bed for a full night.
A five-hour anchor sleep before evening standby — treating tonight as a lost night, because it is.
Standby releases 02:00 and I report 05:00, so I stay at the airport and get two hours in the crew room rather than waste it on a 95-minute drive each way.
Six hours in the afternoon before a fourteen-hour night duty; it's the wrong time of day but it's all there is.
Blackout blinds and an afternoon sleep again — second night in a row, and the debt is building.
Sleep late morning into afternoon after landing at 10:05, then straight back out for the Lisbon nights.
Home at 07:30 local off the last Lisbon; long morning sleep to start clearing four nights of deficit.
Nine hours back on Madrid nights — this is the recovery sleep that actually resets the clock.
Full night before the Singapore sector; I want to be starting that one from a clean tank.
Late-morning nap before a fifteen-hour duty that runs through the entire body night.
Straight to bed on arrival in Singapore after roughly a day awake; six hours, then up for the evening.
Sleeping 04:00–12:00 Singapore local, which is my body night — I'm not shifting for a 33-hour layover.
Two hours before the 21:50 local pickup for another fifteen-hour night home.
Home at 08:45 local; four hours only, so tonight's sleep still lands in the right place.
Full Madrid night to be fit for the Boston departure.
Bed at 16:00 Boston local, which is 22:00 body time — early by local standards but exactly right for me.
Mid-layover nap to bridge a long Boston day without breaking the Madrid clock I need for tomorrow.
The main sleep before the last duty, timed to my body night rather than Boston's.
Short top-up before report, because this duty finishes at 00:15 body time after a 09:00 local start.
Home just before 02:00 local at the end of the roster; sleep in and let it go.

conflicts.statement: The 18SEP standby ends at 02:00Z and the 19SEP DUB turn reports at 05:00Z — three hours nose-to-tail, and with a 95-minute commute each way there is literally no window to go home and sleep.
options: Ask crewing to break the standby-into-duty link or move the DUB turn's report
Do not commute home: stay airside and take a controlled two-hour rest between 02:15Z and 04:15Z
Position to an airport hotel for the 18SEP standby at company expense
Call fatigued before the 05:00Z report rather than after it

conflicts.statement: The 06SEP standby releases at 00:00Z (02:00 local) and the MAD-BOS report is 06:55Z; after two 95-minute commutes that leaves about three and a quarter hours actually in bed.
options: Request release from the 06SEP standby at 22:00Z instead of midnight
Sleep near the airport on the night of the 6th to recover the commute time
Take the 14:00-16:30Z prophylactic nap as planned and declare reduced rest to the operator

conflicts.statement: 19SEP through 21SEP is four duties in a row, each separated by almost exactly ten hours, and every one of them runs through 02:00-06:00 body time; the only sleep available is in the afternoon forbidden zone.
options: Ask for one of the four to be dropped or swapped
Request hotel accommodation at MAD across the block to convert commute time into sleep
Plan in-flight controlled rest on the longer sectors
Track cumulative debt and be ready to call fatigued on the 21SEP Lisbon nights

conflicts.statement: The second 19SEP duty is 14h10 over four sectors, reporting 22:35Z and finishing 12:45Z, i.e. the whole of the night plus the following morning.
options: Query whether this is intended as an augmented crew
Ask crewing to split the FCO and DUB pairings across two days
Confirm with the operator that this is within their FTL scheme before the day

conflicts.statement: Two separate duties are printed against 19SEP with only 10h01 between off-duty at 12:34Z and report at 22:35Z, of which roughly 3h10 is commuting.
options: Confirm the second block really is dated 19SEP and not a print error
Request a hotel at MAD so the ten hours is rest rather than driving
Swap out of one of the two duties

conflicts.statement: Report is 03:05Z (05:05 local Madrid), so the alarm goes at about 02:45 local — a four-sector 11h24 day starting from an almost unsleepable pre-dawn wake-up.
options: Go to bed at 20:00 local on the 12th as planned and accept a short, early-terminated night
Stay in an airport hotel on the night of the 12th to save 95 minutes of commute
Plan a genuine post-duty recovery on the evening of the 13th rather than socialising

conflicts.statement: CV154 reports at 01:50Z, which is 21:50 local Boston, and lands Madrid at midday — the whole duty sits across the body night.
options: Take the planned four-hour Boston afternoon nap rather than staying up
Use in-flight rest if the crew complement allows
Keep the post-arrival nap in Madrid short so the 9th's night sleep still works

conflicts.statement: Both Singapore duties are 15h20 single-sector and each spans the full 02:00-06:00 body-time window; the layover is only about 33 hours, which is too short to shift the body clock.
options: Deliberately stay on Madrid time in Singapore, as planned in the sleep blocks
Confirm augmented crew and bunk allocation for both sectors
Protect the 20:00Z-04:00Z Singapore sleep as non-negotiable

conflicts.statement: 22SEP is shown as a day off but the previous duty does not finish until 03:53Z that morning, so the first hours of the day off are spent getting home and sleeping.
options: Ask whether the day off is credited from 03:53Z or from midnight
Treat 22SEP as recovery only and protect the 21:30Z night sleep
Request the 23SEP CDG turn be moved later if recovery is incomplete

conflicts.statement: Flight numbers are reused within the month for different sectors — CV412 appears as DXB-MAD on 17SEP and MAD-FCO on 19SEP, CV240 as MAD-DUB on 19SEP and BCN-MAD on 20SEP, CV379 as LIS-MAD on 21SEP and CDG-MAD on 23SEP.
options: Confirm the sector routings with crewing before the day rather than relying on flight number
Read the roster by sector pair, not by flight number
Cross-check against the daily flight plan on report
